h: Stories hiding among the flower beds
p: The Botanic Garden was founded in 1621, originally to grow plants for medicine, and you still enter through the grand Danby Gateway, built in the 1630s. Walk through it and you are following in the footsteps of centuries of scientists, students and plant lovers.

Book fans can hunt for a little literary link too. Philip Pullman fans often seek out a bench in the garden that features in the His Dark Materials trilogy, where Lyra and Will promise to meet across their two worlds. It is a lovely, slightly bittersweet spot to sit for a moment.
Allow an hour or two for the city garden. Harcourt Arboretum deserves at least a couple of hours of its own, especially in spring for bluebells or autumn for the colourful acers.
Right opposite the Botanic Garden stands Magdalen College, and Magdalen Bridge is the spot to hire a punt if you fancy a go on the Cherwell yourself.

Harcourt Arboretum sits near the village of Nuneham Courtenay, a few miles south of the city. It is a peaceful spot for a family walk, with plenty of room for kids to roam and some magnificent mature trees to marvel at.
